public_rationale: He says Cursor, Perplexity, Harvey, Lovable and Replit each burn $4 or $5 for every $1 of revenue. None of these private companies publishes total spending or cash burn, and I found no citable report of those ratios for 2025 to early 2026. The figures available are gross margins. Cursor was reportedly at about -23%, meaning serving costs of about 1.23x revenue. Replit's CEO says it has been gross margin positive for over a year. Both make 4 to 5x total spend look doubtful unless their other costs are very large. But gross margin is a different measure from total burn per dollar, so it cannot settle the claim either way. Harvey, Lovable and Perplexity have no usable figures. With no matching data for any of the five, the claim stays unresolved.
limitations: Gross margin is not the same as total spend per dollar of revenue.
Margin figures are CEO claims or press reports, not audited.
He gave no source or period for the ratio.

from_speaker: Cursor, Perplexity, Harvey, Lovable or Replit
burn $4 or $5 for every $1 of revenue
our_interpretation: Plain reading: each named company spends about $4 to $5 in total for each $1 of revenue it earns. Equivalently, losses or cash burn of roughly 3 to 5 times revenue. A ratio well below about 3x total spend to revenue for a company would contradict it for that company.
'These are all' applies the ratio to each of the five companies, not as an average.
Present tense with no period named: I use the latest period public figures could describe before the post, 2025 through Q1 2026.
Gross margin alone does not settle total spend per dollar, but it constrains it.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable figures for each named company (or most of them) showing total spending or cash burn of about 4 to 5 times revenue in 2025 to early 2026.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable figures for one or more named companies showing total spending far below 4 to 5 times revenue, e.g. near break-even or modest losses relative to revenue, in 2025 to early 2026.
